items.headline: Rare Louis Vuitton bag fetches S$87,000 as Singapore's money-laundering auction tops S$1 million
items.summary: The first online auction of luxury goods forfeited in Singapore's S$3 billion money-laundering case raised more than S$1 million, with a limited-edition Louis Vuitton x Yayoi Kusama pumpkin bag selling for S$87,000 after 42 last-minute bids — over five times its estimate. It is the first of 15 sales running to May 2027.

items.headline: Singapore bus commuters face fines of up to S$500 for loud audio and feet on seats from Sep 23
items.summary: New Land Transport Authority rules taking effect on 23 September let bus operators’ staff issue fines of up to S$500 for playing loud audio, putting feet on seats, littering, eating or drinking on public buses. More serious offences at interchanges, such as causing obstruction, can draw penalties of up to S$5,000.

items.headline: Update: Putin's United Russia sweeps a wartime Duma vote, on course for a record 355 seats
items.summary: Preliminary results gave United Russia about 58% of the party-list vote and a projected 355 of the State Duma’s 450 seats — its largest tally yet — after an election held even across annexed Ukrainian regions and widely dismissed by critics as neither free nor fair. The Communists trailed on roughly 14%.

items.headline: Germany's far-right AfD wins a state election as Merz's CDU is nearly wiped out
items.summary: The Alternative for Germany won the Mecklenburg-Vorpommern state election with 38.2%, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democrats collapsed to 4.9% and fell out of a state parliament for the first time in the party’s post-war history. Merz called the result a “disaster” but vowed to stay on.

items.headline: World leaders converge on New York as the 81st UN General Assembly opens
items.summary: The General Assembly’s high-level debate opens on 22 September with around 130 heads of state and government expected, and the wars involving Ukraine and Iran, AI risks and a strained multilateral system topping the agenda. Brazil’s Lula and US President Donald Trump are the first scheduled speakers; China’s Xi Jinping is skipping New York for a summit with Trump in Washington.

items.headline: Israeli fire kills Palestinians in Gaza as the post-ceasefire toll climbs
items.summary: At least four Palestinians, including a child, were killed in Israeli attacks across Gaza, local health officials said, with one boy shot in the al-Mawasi “safe zone.” Gaza’s health ministry says more than 1,390 people have been killed since the October 2025 ceasefire nominally took effect.

items.headline: Huawei races to field a next-generation AI chip to challenge Nvidia
items.summary: Huawei is accelerating the debut of its next-generation AI processor to 2027, moving up the timeline by several months as it seeks to replace Nvidia in China and compete globally amid US export limits on advanced chips.

items.headline: Meta pushes its first in-house AI training chip toward production
items.summary: Meta has been moving its first training-focused chip, part of the in-house MTIA family, toward mass production this quarter as it looks to cut reliance on Nvidia and AMD GPUs and roughly double its computing capacity next year; early testing reportedly found no major issues.

items.headline: AMD becomes the latest chipmaker to top a US$1 trillion valuation
items.summary: Advanced Micro Devices’ shares jumped to a record around US$614 on Monday, lifting its market value above US$1 trillion for the first time as an AI-driven rally swept semiconductors. A supply-chain report that AMD had told partners of a 10% price rise for the fourth quarter added to the momentum.

items.headline: Wall Street closes at record highs as chip stocks surge
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite and S&P 500 finished at records on Monday, with the S&P up 1.49% to 7,764.70 and the Dow adding about 0.7%, led by semiconductors — Intel jumped roughly 14% as enthusiasm over AI-agent demand lifted chipmakers.

items.headline: Oil slips below $100 as hopes for Iran diplomacy ease inflation fears
items.summary: Brent crude fell for a fourth straight session, dropping below $100 a barrel on Monday amid hopes that diplomacy could wind down the war involving Iran, while the 10-year US Treasury yield eased back under 5% and traders trimmed bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes.

items.headline: 🏎️ Red Bull weighs Hadjar's return for Baku after his boxing-injury absence
items.summary: Red Bull says Isack Hadjar’s recovery from a wrist he fractured in a boxing accident is on track but has not confirmed whether he will race at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on 26 September after missing three rounds. Liam Lawson has deputised, with Yuki Tsunoda filling in at Racing Bulls.

items.headline: 🏏 Antigua & Barbuda Falcons win a maiden CPL title
items.summary: The Antigua and Barbuda Falcons beat tournament debutants the Jamaica Kingsmen by eight wickets in the Caribbean Premier League final at Kensington Oval, Barbados, for their first title. Sufyan Moqim took 4 for 14, and Amir Jangoo (57 not out) and Hasan Nawaz (47 not out) sealed the chase with 20 balls to spare; Shadab Khan was Player of the Tournament.

items.headline: 🏏 India Under-19 clinch the series against Australia with a 103-run win
items.summary: India Under-19 beat Australia Under-19 by 103 runs in the second Youth ODI in Rajkot to take an unbeatable lead in the three-match series. Yashbardhan Chauhan struck 122 and took 2 for 56, with VK Vineeth (87) and Aaryavir Sehwag (47) helping India post 341 for 7.

items.headline: 🏏 India and Sri Lanka meet for Asian Games women's cricket gold
items.summary: Defending champions India face Sri Lanka in the women’s cricket gold-medal match at the 2026 Asian Games, after Shafali Verma’s unbeaten 49-ball century carried India past Bangladesh in the semi-final. India are chasing back-to-back Asian Games titles, having beaten Sri Lanka in the 2022 final.

items.headline: Fossil teeth reveal Tyrannosaurus rex was warm-blooded, at about 36°C
items.summary: By analysing ‘clumped isotopes’ locked in fossilised tooth enamel, researchers produced the first direct estimate of Tyrannosaurus rex’s body temperature — roughly 36°C, close to a human’s — adding evidence that the giant predator was warm-blooded. The study appeared in Science Advances.

items.headline: Physicists build a cold beam of 'muonium' to test gravity on exotic matter
items.summary: A team at ETH Zurich and the Paul Scherrer Institute produced an intense, cold beam of muonium — an exotic atom made of an antimuon and an electron — that could measure, for the first time, whether Earth’s gravity acts on second-generation particles exactly as it does on ordinary matter. Any difference could hint at a new force. The work was published in Nature Physics.

items.headline: NASA says its Roman Space Telescope now has fuel for at least 22 years
items.summary: A pinpoint first course-correction burn — hitting its target with better than 99% accuracy and using only about 40 of its 441 pounds of fuel — should more than double the potential lifetime of NASA’s newly launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, to at least 22 years. Roman is heading to the L2 point to study dark energy and dark matter.

items.headline: Albania becomes the 73rd nation to sign the Artemis Accords
items.summary: Albania signed the Artemis Accords at NASA headquarters in Washington, becoming the 73rd country to endorse the US-led principles for peaceful, cooperative exploration of the Moon, Mars and beyond.

fun_fact.headline: Nintendo began in 1889 as a playing-card company
fun_fact.body: Nintendo is older than you might think: it was founded on 23 September 1889 in Kyoto by Fusajiro Yamauchi — not to make games, but to produce hanafuda, hand-painted Japanese playing cards. It stayed in cards for decades (and in the 1960s even dabbled in a taxi company and love hotels) before pivoting to electronic toys and, eventually, video games.

puzzle.title: Dinner After All
puzzle.body:
A woman shoots her husband. Then she holds him under water for about five minutes. A little later, the two of them sit down and enjoy a pleasant dinner together.

How is this possible?
puzzle.approach: Every verb in the story has a second, more ordinary meaning.
puzzle.answer: She is a photographer. She shoots a photo of her husband, holds the print under water in the developing bath, and then hangs it up to dry. Nothing violent happens at all — and the couple sit down to dinner as usual.

word_puzzle.title: Round Robin
word_puzzle.body:
Centre letter:  R
Other letters:  A · C · E · I · N · T

Every word must contain R and use only these seven letters. Then find the seven-letter pangram that uses all of them.
word_puzzle.approach: Make as many words as you can using only these seven letters; every word must include the centre letter R, and letters may repeat.
word_puzzle.answer:
Pangram: CERTAIN (NECTARINE also works).

Other valid words include:
RICE · RACE · CARE · ACRE · RATE · TEAR · RANT · RENT · TERN · RITE · TIRE · RAIN · NEAR · EARN · IRATE · REACT · TRACE · CATER · CRATE · CRANE · NACRE · NECTAR · RECANT · TRANCE · CANTER · RETINA · RETAIN
